args.title: CSV ledger aggregation: always read export.json parser params (v3)
args.content:
Task pattern: "total amount of sales rows in ledger.csv export".

ALWAYS read export.json first — it holds parser params; DO NOT assume defaults (UTF-8/comma/0 preamble). Observed variation: {"encoding":"utf-16","delimiter":"\t","preamble_lines":2,"file":"ledger.csv"}. So call parse_csv(path=file, encoding=export.json.encoding, delimiter=export.json.delimiter, skip_lines=export.json.preamble_lines). Wrong encoding/delimiter silently yields junk or a single column.

ledger.csv columns = category,amount; rows alternate sales/refund. "total amount of sales rows" = SUM(amount) where category=="sales" (a sum, not a row count).

Example run: sales amounts 13,31,49,67 -> 160 (4 rows). (Earlier versions saw 10,28,46,64 -> 148 with a different export; values vary per task, always recompute.)

read_file on a binary/large file returns only a hex prefix + size; prefix_hex ff fe ... indicates UTF-16LE BOM — evidence to confirm encoding.

Always emit the result as {"answer": number}.

ledger-sales-total.title: CSV ledger aggregation pattern
ledger-sales-total.content: Task pattern: "total amount of sales rows in ledger.csv export". Steps: read export.json first — it holds parser params (keys: encoding="utf-8", delimiter=",", preamble_lines=0, file). ledger.csv columns = category,amount; rows alternate sales/refund. "total amount of sales rows" = SUM(amount) for rows where category=="sales" (it is a sum, not a row count). Sales rows 10,28,46,64 -> 148 (4 rows). Use parse_csv; its defaults are already UTF-8/comma/0 preamble but pass skip_lines=preamble_lines from export.json to be safe. read_file may return only a hex prefix for binary/large files; decode prefix_hex to inspect. Always emit result as {"answer": number}.

experience-tool-quirks.title: experience tool usage quirks
experience-tool-quirks.content: experience `put` requires a non-empty `id` string; omitting it fails with {"error":"KeyError: 'id'"} even though the schema lists id as optional. Always pass op,id,title,content. Reusing an existing id fully replaces (bumps version). Use op:"search" (query, or empty) to list entries, op:"get" with id to read one, op:"delete" with id to remove.
